# ClassMethodNameMatchesFieldName

<Badge type="info" text="info" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Confusing constructs](/rules/#confusing-constructs) · PhpStorm name: `ClassMethodNameMatchesFieldNameInspection`

When a method and a property share a name, `$obj->name()` and
`($obj->name)()` mean different things. This is especially confusing when the
property holds a callable, and when the property's type is unknown the reader
cannot tell which one is meant.

## Example

```php{4,12,13,17}
<?php
class Account {
    private $owner;
    public function owner() {}
}

class Hooks {
    /* @var callable */
    protected $onSave;
    /** @var \Closure|null */
    protected $onLoad;
    public function onSave() {}
    public static function onLoad() {}
}

class Child extends Account {
    public function owner() {}
}

class Counter {
    private $total = 0;
    private ?string $label;
    const size = 3;
    public function total() {}
    public function label() {}
    public function size() {}
}

interface Named {
    public function name();
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 4: A property with this name exists and its type is unknown; rename the method or type the property.</li>
<li>line 12: A callable property with this name exists; rename the method (for example with a get/is/has prefix).</li>
<li>line 13: A callable property with this name exists; rename the method (for example with a get/is/has prefix).</li>
<li>line 17: A property with this name exists and its type is unknown; rename the method or type the property.</li>
</ul>

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ClassMethodNameMatchesFieldName": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file), either of:

```php
// @custos-ignore ClassMethodNameMatchesFieldName

/**
 * @noinspection ClassMethodNameMatchesFieldNameInspection
 */
```
